samples.summary: Current-slide listeners now fire from inside `editor.render()`, so host callbacks (Yorkie presence writes) run on the RAF tick and inside the store's own change notification — an unguarded new failure mode
samples.evidence: `resolveCurrentSlide` (editor.ts:1572) fires `currentSlideListeners` and clears selection/cell-selection from inside `render()`/`repaintOverlay()`. Previously these listeners only fired from user-driven `setCurrentSlide` (editor.ts:1516) or `setStore` (1642). The desktop host subscribes `broadcast` to that channel (slides-view.tsx:1094), and `broadcast` writes to the collaborative document via `store.updatePresence(...)` (slides-view.tsx:1079). That write is now reachable (a) from the per-frame RAF loop `tick()` at slides-view.tsx:1110-1123, which calls `editor.render()` with no try/catch — anything thrown by a listener (e.g. a presence write on a disposed/detached Yorkie doc) escapes `render()` and the loop is never re-scheduled, permanently freezing the canvas; and (b) re-entrantly from inside a Yorkie `remote-change` subscription callback via `store.onChange` → `editor.render()` (slides-view.tsx:1051-1053, yorkie-slides-store.ts:364-369), i.e. a `doc.update` opened from within a document event callback. The fix belongs on the new code: defer the heal's listener notification / interaction teardown out of the paint path, or guard the RAF tick.

samples.summary: Mobile view's own cursor reconciler overrides the heal's choice, so the same removal lands on a different slide than on desktop
samples.evidence: mobile-slides-view.tsx:183-191 resets React `currentSlideId` to `snapshot.slideIds[0]` whenever the held id disappears from the store, and the effect at mobile-slides-view.tsx:451-457 pushes that back into the editor with `editor.setCurrentSlide(...)`. So after an undone `Add slide` / peer delete, the mobile editor ends on the FIRST slide, not on the `currentIndex - 1` slide the new heal picks (editor.ts:1554) — and the heal's own notification (`onCurrentSlideChange`, mobile-slides-view.tsx:424-428) will race with it. Mobile edit mode also has no `store.onChange → editor.render()` wiring (only the mount-time `editor.render()` at line 389), so on that mount the heal may not even run before React's reconciler wins.

samples.summary: Thumbnail-panel delete now double-moves the cursor: the heal preempts it synchronously inside `store.batch()`'s change notification
samples.evidence: thumbnail-panel.ts:302-323 picks its own survivor (`first surviving slide AFTER the anchor`) and calls `editor.setCurrentSlide(nextCurrent)` after `store.batch(() => store.removeSlides(...))`. On the desktop host the batch's notification runs `editor.render()` synchronously (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053), so the new heal fires first and moves the cursor to `currentIndex - 1`, clears the selection, cancels any anchored text edit, and notifies subscribers (editor.ts:1561-1572) — then the panel moves the cursor again to a *different* slide. Net result is two current-slide notifications (hence two presence writes) and an intermediate cursor the panel did not intend; the panel's own survivor policy is now dead weight for the common single-delete case.

samples.summary: Healing is reachable only through the two paint paths; `getCurrentSlideId()` and every non-paint `currentId` consumer still hand out / act on the dangling id
samples.evidence: `resolveCurrentSlide` is called only from `repaintOverlay()` (editor.ts:1082) and `render()` (editor.ts:1440). `getCurrentSlideId()` (editor.ts:1500) still returns the raw `currentId`, and other internal consumers keep their own unhealed lookups: `currentSlide()` (editor.ts:5619-5623), `previewAnimations()` (editor.ts:2686-2688), `insertTable()` (editor.ts:1798), `computePeerCursors(this.peers, this.currentId)` (editor.ts:1305). External consumers that read the id between a mutation and the next paint therefore still see a slide the deck no longer holds — e.g. packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/slide-group.tsx:33-37 (falls back to appending the new slide at the end of the deck), packages/slides/src/view/editor/thumbnail-panel.ts:305 and :642-644, packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1188 (`prevSlideIdRef` seeded from a possibly-dangling id). Healing inside `getCurrentSlideId()` (or a shared resolver) would close the gap.

verdict.reason: Every cited location checks out. `resolveCurrentSlide` fires `currentSlideListeners` at editor.ts:1572 (plus tears down crop/edit/cell-selection at 1568-1571) and is called from the paint path — `render()` at editor.ts:1440 and `repaintOverlay()` at editor.ts:1082 — so current-slide listeners now run inside a paint. The desktop host subscribes `broadcast` to that channel at slides-view.tsx:1094, and `broadcast` performs a collaborative-document write via `store.updatePresence(...)` at slides-view.tsx:1079-1091, which lands on `this.doc.update((_, p) => p.set(presence))` at yorkie-slides-store.ts:2751 when no batch is open. Consequently: (a) the RAF loop at slides-view.tsx:1110-1123 calls `editor.render()` (line 1115) with no try/catch and only reschedules at line 1121, so anything thrown by a listener escapes `render()` and permanently freezes the canvas; (b) `store.onChange` at slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 calls `editor.render()`, and those listeners are dispatched from inside the Yorkie `remote-change` subscription callback at yorkie-slides-store.ts:364-369, so a presence `doc.update` is now opened re-entrantly from within a document event callback. `render()` itself guards only `this.disposed` (editor.ts:1402), and no caller wraps it, so nothing makes this unreachable. `notifyChange`'s try/catch (yorkie-slides-store.ts:393-396) blunts error escape on path (b) only and does not cover the RAF path or the re-entrancy. This is squarely in the blast-radius lane — a behaviour change to the exported `render()` contract (previously a pure paint) whose other consumers (tick loop, onChange handler, and other current-slide subscribers at thumbnail-panel.ts:622, notes-panel.ts:104, motion-panel/index.tsx:28, background-side-panel.tsx:47) were not adjusted. Heal branch is reachable by design (peer deletes current slide / undo of add-slide). Major.

mergedFrom.summary: Two competing cursor policies for the same slide-removal event: the thumbnail panel's Delete slide picks the first SURVIVOR AFTER the anchor, the new heal picks the slide BEFORE the vanished index

finding.summary: Thumbnail-panel delete now double-moves the cursor: the heal fires first (backwards) and its own survivor choice (forwards) second
finding.evidence: thumbnail-panel.ts:320-323 does `store.batch(() => store.removeSlides([...targetIds]))` and only afterwards `editor.setCurrentSlide(nextCurrent)`. The batch notifies store listeners synchronously, and packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 responds with `editor.markDirty(); editor.render();` — which now runs `resolveCurrentSlide` and heals the cursor to `currentIndex - 1` (the slide BEFORE the deleted one), firing `currentSlideListeners` (presence broadcast at slides-view.tsx:1073-1094, thumbnail highlight, notes panel, toolbar refresh) and clearing selection. Line 321-322 then moves the cursor a second time to the panel's intended survivor (the first surviving slide AFTER the anchor, lines 315-318). Net effect for the user: a visible one-frame jump to the wrong slide, two `onCurrentSlideChange` notifications and two presence writes per delete. The delete path should either be made heal-aware or the heal should reuse the same survivor rule.

verdict.reason: Verified the whole chain in-repo. thumbnail-panel.ts:302-326 computes `nextCurrent` (first survivor AFTER the anchor, lines 315-318), commits the delete via `store.batch(...)` at line 320, and only then calls `editor.setCurrentSlide(nextCurrent)` at 321-323. The batch notifies listeners synchronously in the same turn (memory.ts:1789-1803 with notifyChange at 1783-1787; production path yorkie-slides-store.ts:598-630 calling notifyChange at 628, dispatch at 393-397). The subscriber at slides-view.tsx:1051-1059 runs `editor.markDirty(); editor.render();`, and markDirty itself calls repaintOverlay (editor.ts:2658-2669) which resolves at editor.ts:1082, with render resolving again at editor.ts:1440. With currentId dangling, resolveCurrentSlide (editor.ts:1538-1574) heals BACKWARDS to currentIndex-1 (line 1554), rewrites currentId (1561), clears cell + element selection (1570-1571) and fires currentSlideListeners (1572). setCurrentSlide's early-return only triggers on an exact id match (editor.ts:1505), and the healed id (slide before) differs from nextCurrent (slide after the anchor), so the cursor moves a second time and notifies listeners again (editor.ts:1516). Both notifications reach the presence broadcast subscribed at slides-view.tsx:1094 (broadcast body 1073-1092), so one delete yields two cursor resolutions and two presence writes. Reachability is confirmed: the panel is mounted with the same store/editor instances that own the onChange listener (slides-view.tsx:1014-1019). This is a behaviour change to a shared symbol (the editor's cursor-resolve contract) breaking an out-of-diff consumer plus a violated one-move-per-delete invariant — squarely in the blast-radius lane, and nothing guards or short-circuits the double move.

finding.summary: `render()` is no longer side-effect-free: it can now clear selection, cancel text editing, discard a crop session and notify listeners — and it is called synchronously from a store-change callback
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1059 calls `editor.render()` directly inside `store.onChange`. The heal path (editor.ts:1544-1554) re-enters `exitEditMode('cancel')` → `finishEditMode()` → `render()`/`repaintOverlay()` (editor.ts:4576-4591) and fires `currentSlideListeners`, whose frontend handler writes presence back into the store (`broadcast` → `store.updatePresence`, slides-view.tsx:1073-1080). Callers that assumed painting cannot mutate editor/store state (this one, board-view.tsx:557/717, mobile-slides-view.tsx:389, refitCanvas at slides-view.tsx:872-873) were not reviewed for that re-entrancy; `updatePresence` only guards the in-batch case (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2748-2752), so I could not confirm every notify path lands outside an open `doc.update`. Also note uncommitted text is discarded here while every other cursor-move path (`setCurrentSlide` editor.ts:1494, `setStore` editor.ts:1606) commits.
